End of the Redisa Empire

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Five years ago Carte Blanche raised the red flag about Redisa. Finally the minister has responded and Redisa's party is coming to an end

Unique Selling Point:
We have been on the story for the past five years and have the inside track on the latest developments that vindicate our story by a cabinet minister

Summary:
On the 30th May, Minister Edna Molewa left for Brazil. When she arrived, she had an urgent matter to attend to at the SA consulate in Sao Paulo. She was about to sign nearly 300 pages of an urgent notice of motion to liquidate Redisa, the tyre recycling plan led by its CEO Hermann Erdmann. By signing the papers the minister began a process to dismantle the plan that she had signed into being in 2012 and defended vigorously until Carte Blanche exposed Redisa for the sham it was in 2015



Further information:
The minister was so concerned about the public funds that she told the court that she had reason to believe that Erdmann would contravene the plan by dissipating public funds still under its control as well as the assets of Redisa. “I fear” says the minister “that large amounts of public funds have already been misappropriated”

The court granted the provisional liquidation order and on Friday the 2nd June the liquidators marched into the plush Redisa offices, froze the bank accounts and took control of the tyre recycling plan. As it turned out Redisa’s Erdmann, had been trying to move over R200 million rand out of the bank accounts. The DEA and the liquidators stopped some of the money transfers but not all of them. But it looks like the party is over for Erdmann and his coterie of directors who have lived it up over the last three years, courtesy of the South African taxpayer.

But the minister was not yet finished with Hermann Erdmann and his directors. Each year a private for profit management company Kusaga Taka takes around 20% or about a R100 million a year to manage the operations of the tyre recycling plan. Since our expose in 2015, DDG Mark Gordon has been trying to get the contract between Redisa and KT and a number of other documents. Redisa has flat out refused. But it’s in this company where the bodies are buried and so on Friday the 9th June the court granted the DEA a second provisional liquidation of Kusaga Taka. Reliable sources confirm that Erdmann had a fit and had to be escorted out of the Sunclaire offices on Friday afternoon. But more is to come as revelations from the DEA’s investigations are revealed.

Carte Blanche updates this 5 year investigation as it appears that Erdmann and his directors are running out of options.

Redisa 2017 final script

Commentary One
In late 2012 minister Edna Molewa brought to life a tyre recycling plan called Redisa.
Redisa had 5 years to enable busy industries that would create new products from old tyres. By now, we should see ten thousand disadvantaged people lifted out of poverty- That is what is gazetted in the minister’s plan, and what it’s CEO, Hermann Erdmann promised to do

Devi
So, in five years it should run at optimum level?
Hermann
Absolutely! We hope to do that earlier

Commentary Two
But what’s happened, is that the directors have made themselves fabulously wealthy and the minister has had to confront facts. Redisa has gone rogue

Vanessa
She had this dream of waste to worth. To create…. and to find out that there were only a few individuals that benefitted. It disgusted our minister.

Commentary Three
Vanessa Bedeman has led the charge against Redisa for the department of environment. At the Cape High court, Redisa’s counsel have battled it out against the DEA, as the minister asked the court to liquidate Redisa.

Judge Henney
The volume of this record runs to 4000 pages. This court has prepared a comprehensive judgement

Vanessa
Redisa underestimated the ability of government, we have spent sleepless nights going through the documents to get to this point. it was not an easy task

Commentary Four
For the last 4.5 years Redisa has collected R2.30 per kilogram for every tyre or casing imported into, or manufactured in South Africa. Put another way, taxes on your tyres have, since 2013, totaled R2.2 billion and gone straight into the bank account of this public benefit organisation

Devi to Vanessa
Would you say Redisa achieved its aim?
Vanessa
Not at all. They missed their targets completely


Commentary Five
We first met Hermann Erdmann in 2012 when he successfully fended off a legal challenge to his plan

Devi 2012
Redisa has been accused of being a money- making scheme?
Hermann
We have the highest auditing standards. We have been transparent. Come in and see us, ask the question and we will supply it

Commentary six
We met again in October 2014, when allegations filtered through to us that the directors, Hermann Erdmann, Charlie Kirk and Stacey Davidson were living like millionaires on our tyre tax

Devi to Hermann
Do you think people have dialed you up wrong?
Hermann
I think so …I speak to governments all over the world…the prophet in his own land is often not popular

Commentary seven
Redisa is a non- profit company. The profits would be earned by Kusaga Taka, the management company that would run Redisa for an 18% fee. Chris Crozier would be KT’s CEO. Behind that, was a second company, Nine- years Investments, and according to court documents, these companies would later siphon off huge amounts of public money from Redisa. But back in 2014, all we knew was that Erdmann was both a director of Redisa and a shareholder of Kusaga Taka

Up sound Conflict of interest
Devi
What is your shareholding in KT?
Hermann Erdmann
I own part of the company …

Commentary eight
In 2015 our story exposed how Redisa was misleading the Department on job stats, how they were exporting whole tyres instead of creating industries here at home, and how Erdmann had moved from his comfortable Lonehill home to one of the most expensive homes in the Cape.

Commentary nine
Redisa was furious about the story, and sent a 260- page complaint to the Broadcast complaints commission. Dr. Dario Milo has been defending Carte Blanche against Redisa ever since.

LINK
After our expose in 2015 the department launched an investigation into Redisa. It was supposed to take three months but throughout 2016 the department battled to get documents out of Redisa

Vanessa
They would give you a contract – it was the front and the back of the contract and there were pages missing or it was not signed or irrelevant. We had boxes delivered to the department, but none of it made sense

Commentary ten
By October 2016 the minister had run out of patience and sent Redisa a letter giving them 15 days to furnish her with reasons why she shouldn’t cancel the plan. Once again, we reported on Redisa’s apparent extravagance

Devi and Jan
Shamwari game reserve R194 000.

Commentary eleven
Once again Dario Milo received yet another BCCSA complaint against Carte Blanche

Vanessa
The ministers biggest concern was there was no governance, and there was no oversight and they claimed accountability, they claimed transparency, but it was malicious compliance right through.

Commentary Twelve
But before the minister could act, she needed proof, and commissioned this performance review. It was a damning. But Erdmann denied the claims, so the DEA asked Ernst &Young to do a review of the review.

Vanessa
From the time that Isolveit started their performance review, we realized there is something very wrong at Redisa

Commentary Thirteen
What was wrong at Redisa’s head office in Claremont, was a complete absence of corporate governance. Directors violated their own Memorandum of incorporation, procurement policies were flouted. But Redisa paid almost R20 million rand to PR company Fleishman Hillard to spin their story. Meanwhile waste pickers were trying to scrape together a living on R2 per tyre.

Terence
We realized we couldn’t even buy bread




Commentary Fourteen
Erdmann and his directors saw Redisa as a stepping stone. They had his sights set on a far more valuable prize -control of the entire countries waste streams-lightbulbs, paper and packaging, general waste, electronic waste.

Hermann Erdmann
We are not working in the tyre industry we are working in the waste stream industry.

Commentary Fifteen
The Redisa plan legally restricted Erdmann to the recycling of tyres in South Africa only. But Erdmann’s ambitions over- rode this detail. From Australia to Albania – Erdmann was planning world tyre recycling domination

Devi
Cos you want to expand
Hermann
Yes, absolutely we want to expand.

Commentary Sixteen
But at home treasury was about to spoil the Redisa party. From February this year SARS, and not Redisa was legislated to collect the funds from the tyre industry. So Redisa did what they always seem to do- they took Treasury and DEA to court

VANESSA
They were obviously very opposed to the money being collected by SARS and you can see why.

LINK
Then suddenly in May this year they said they were running out of cash and they would have to stop collecting tyres

Vanessa
What Redisa tried to do was hold the minister to ransom by stopping collections

Commentary Seventeen
Redisa was burning through R36 million a month. Its reserves had shrunk from seven months to just more than a week.

Devi
And the money was flying out of the account
Vanessa
Yes it was flying out of account, the industry was going to be left in the lurch

Commentary Eighteen
To protect the dwindling funds, the ministers legal team advised her to ask the High Court to put Redisa into provisional liquidation.

Link
The minister was so concerned about the money, that she told the court that “
millions of rand is at stake and I fear, she says “that large amounts of public funds have already been misappropriated

Commentary nineteen
The Court agreed with the minister and in June granted the provisional liquidation. Redisa fought on, but on the 15th of September Judge Henney sealed Redisa’s fate in the high court case, when he put both Redisa, but Kusaga Taka into final liquidation

Up Sound Henney
I order that the respondent be placed in final liquidation

Vanessa Up sound
…. we had suspicions, now with the forensic investigator that was appointed by the liquidator all our suspicions have been confirmed

LINK
About R2 billion rand has poured into Redisa’s coffers since it began – that is around R600 million a year. But where has all the money gone

Commentary twenty
These reports by the forensic investigators are not yet final, and updated as more evidence comes to light.

Vanessa
They were using the bank account at Redisa as if it was their personal bank account

Commentary twenty- one
Chairman of the board Xolani Qubeka was excessively overpaid say the investigators and could not be independent. Over R12 months he was paid R1.5 million and was only required to attend 5 board meetings a year. Redisa also paid his rent of over half a million rand.
Erdmann was also earning a huge salary. In January 2013, it started at R140 000. But he balked when we held him to his promise of transparency

Devi
But Hermann if I am paying you a fee, I think I have a right to know what you are doing with the money
Hermann
Ya but you can’t tell me how much are you getting paid from Redisa
Devi
Yes, but I am contributing to your salary. I know what President Zuma is earning
Hermann
Yes but I am not president Zuma and I don’t work for government
Devi
So the answer is you are not very transparent
Hermann
Well that is your opinion

Vanessa
As of May 2017 his salary was in excess of R340 000 per month – an increase of approximately 102% and 267% more than CPI, so he must have performed extremely well unfortunately the department and the minister could not see that

Commentary twenty- two
As the money poured in Redisa bought this R18 million rand Sandton apartment and spent another R5 million to upgrade it. Erdmann moved his family from one exclusive Cape Suburb to another. Fresnay it appears, then over the mountain to Bishops court where Redisa paid the lease. Last year Erdmann’s trust paid R25.5 million for this Constantia home and Redisa coughed up for the private security for directors Erdmann and Davidson

Vanessa
The extent of the expenses in terms of the security upgrades more than R2.2 million
Devi
That is very good security
Vanessa
This is just the tip of the iceberg in terms of money misappropriated

LINK
In her paper’s the minister speaks about staggering amounts of money and she is not exaggerating.

Commentary twenty-three
Charlie Kirk bought an ocean- going yacht. Erdmann has one too. Easy to afford for Erdmann who funneled R97 million rand in dividends to himself through nine years Investments. But in his affidavit Erdmann asserts “ I receive no more than my salary”

But through nine years the directors awarded themselves R121. 6 million rand in dividends and royalties. Erdmann has always bragged about the computer system

Up sound Erdmann
You know I speak to lots of governments around the world and I said when last did you switch on a computer system that actually worked.

Commentary twenty four
The NCCS should work. It cost us R76 million. But the investigators discovered that the directors hijacked the IP and the system into their own for- profit companies

Vanessa
But wait there is more. We then discovered that royalties were paid from KT to Nine years for the utilization of the system.

Commentary twenty- five
With royalties your tyre tax funded a R97 million system

Vanessa
After all that money that was spent we find out that the system didn’t work

Commentary twenty- six
Erdmann wanted the computer system to accommodate the waste stream contracts he hoped to get. But to bag that prize he appeared to need help from his friends. Enoch Godongwana, head of the ANC transformation committee’s company Isivuno came up in the investigation

Vanessa
The minister has made it clear she wants the investigation to take its course, so that will be followed as well.

Commentary twenty seven
Redisa have paid Godongwana R100 000 per month since 2014. Had he landed Redisa the waste streams, Godongwana stood to gain a R3 million rand success fee for general waste, another three million for mine water drainage, three million for E waste, one million for household light globes and three million for rehabilitation of mines. Godongwana has not replied to our questions. Meanwhile KPMG was giving Redisa unqualified audits year after year

Hermann
We have had two clean audits by KPMG so we are very happy with what we are doing

Commentary twenty eight
But The investigators have found KPMG have ignored numerous reportable irregularities.
KPMG have not yet responded to our questions.

Vanessa
We had a team of highly dedicated officials that want to see that public funds are utilized where they are supposed to be utilized

Commentary twenty nine
Redisa say the judgement is legally flawed and is being appealed, and the preliminary forensic reports are factually incorrect in virtually all respects. But the DEA are not standing down

Vanessa
we have lodged a complaint with the hawks and its being investigated
Devi
Will you go after the money?
Vanessa
We will! it’s a huge amount of Money Devi – there is no way they can get away with that!

THE END 14 02


PROMO ONE 10
Redisa was meant to create 10 000 jobs and a recycling industry, but on Friday Minister Edna molewa formally revoked Redisa’s tyre recycling plan

PROMO TWO
Devi to Vanessa
Would you say Redisa achieved its aim?
Vanessa
Not at all. They missed their targets completely

Commentary
Carte Blanche brings you the latest chapter on the Redisa tyre recycling story.


PROMO THREE
Hermann Erdmann is the CEO of Redisa. He has always maintained the tyre recycling plan is achieving its targets and the directors have been transparent

Yes, but I am contributing to your salary. I know what President Zuma is earning
Hermann
Yes but I am not president Zuma and I don’t work for government
Devi
So the answer is you are not very transparent
Hermann
Well that is your opinion

Redisa fought on, but on the 15th of September Judge Henney sealed Redisa’s fate in the high court case, when he put both Redisa, but Kusaga Taka into final liquidation Up Sound Henney I order that the respondent be placed in final liquidation Vanessa Up sound …. we had suspicions, now with the forensic investigator that was appointed by the liquidator all our suspicions have been confirmed LINK About R2 billion rand has poured into Redisa’s coffers since it began – that is around R600 million a year. But where has all the money gone Commentary twenty These reports by the forensic investigators are not yet final, and updated as more evidence comes to light. Vanessa They were using the bank account at Redisa as if it was their personal bank account Commentary twenty- one Chairman of the board Xolani Qubeka was excessively overpaid say the investigators and could not be independent. Over R12 months he was paid R1.5 million and was only required to attend 5 board meetings a year. Redisa also paid his rent of over half a million rand. Erdmann was also earning a huge salary. In January 2013, it started at R140 000. But he balked when we held him to his promise of transparency Devi But Hermann if I am paying you a fee, I think I have a right to know what you are doing with the money Hermann Ya but you can’t tell me how much are you getting paid from Redisa Devi Yes, but I am contributing to your salary. I know what President Zuma is earning Hermann Yes but I am not president Zuma and I don’t work for government Devi So the answer is you are not very transparent Hermann Well that is your opinion Vanessa As of May 2017 his salary was in excess of R340 000 per month – an increase of approximately 102% and 267% more than CPI, so he must have performed extremely well unfortunately the department and the minister could not see that Commentary twenty- two As the money poured in Redisa bought this R18 million rand Sandton apartment and spent another R5 million to upgrade it. Erdmann moved his family from one exclusive Cape Suburb to another. Fresnay it appears, then over the mountain to Bishops court where Redisa paid the lease. Last year Erdmann’s trust paid R25.5 million for this Constantia home and Redisa coughed up for the private security for directors Erdmann and Davidson Vanessa The extent of the expenses in terms of the security upgrades more than R2.2 million Devi That is very good security Vanessa This is just the tip of the iceberg in terms of money misappropriated LINK In her paper’s the minister speaks about staggering amounts of money and she is not exaggerating. Commentary twenty-three Charlie Kirk bought an ocean- going yacht. Erdmann has one too. Easy to afford for Erdmann who funneled R97 million rand in dividends to himself through nine years Investments. But in his affidavit Erdmann asserts “ I receive no more than my salary” But through nine years the directors awarded themselves R121. 6 million rand in dividends and royalties. Erdmann has always bragged about the computer system Up sound Erdmann You know I speak to lots of governments around the world and I said when last did you switch on a computer system that actually worked. Commentary twenty four The NCCS should work. It cost us R76 million. But the investigators discovered that the directors hijacked the IP and the system into their own for- profit companies Vanessa But wait there is more. We then discovered that royalties were paid from KT to Nine years for the utilization of the system. Commentary twenty- five With royalties your tyre tax funded a R97 million system Vanessa After all that money that was spent we find out that the system didn’t work Commentary twenty- six Erdmann wanted the computer system to accommodate the waste stream contracts he hoped to get. But to bag that prize he appeared to need help from his friends. Enoch Godongwana, head of the ANC transformation committee’s company Isivuno came up in the investigation Vanessa The minister has made it clear she wants the investigation to take its course, so that will be followed as well. Commentary twenty seven Redisa have paid Godongwana R100 000 per month since 2014. Had he landed Redisa the waste streams, Godongwana stood to gain a R3 million rand success fee for general waste, another three million for mine water drainage, three million for E waste, one million for household light globes and three million for rehabilitation of mines. Godongwana has not replied to our questions. Meanwhile KPMG was giving Redisa unqualified audits year after year Hermann We have had two clean audits by KPMG so we are very happy with what we are doing Commentary twenty eight But The investigators have found KPMG have ignored numerous reportable irregularities. KPMG have not yet responded to our questions. Vanessa We had a team of highly dedicated officials that want to see that public funds are utilized where they are supposed to be utilized Commentary twenty nine Redisa say the judgement is legally flawed and is being appealed, and the preliminary forensic reports are factually incorrect in virtually all respects. But the DEA are not standing down Vanessa we have lodged a complaint with the hawks and its being investigated Devi Will you go after the money? Vanessa We will! it’s a huge amount of Money Devi – there is no way they can get away with that! THE END 14 02 PROMO ONE 10 Redisa was meant to create 10 000 jobs and a recycling industry, but on Friday Minister Edna molewa formally revoked Redisa’s tyre recycling plan PROMO TWO Devi to Vanessa Would you say Redisa achieved its aim? Vanessa Not at all. They missed their targets completely Commentary Carte Blanche brings you the latest chapter on the Redisa tyre recycling story. PROMO THREE Hermann Erdmann is the CEO of Redisa. He has always maintained the tyre recycling plan is achieving its targets and the directors have been transparent Yes, but I am contributing to your salary. I know what President Zuma is earning Hermann Yes but I am not president Zuma and I don’t work for government Devi So the answer is you are not very transparent Hermann Well that is your opinion Invoicing Back references from Insert ID in Invoice: Title Author Last Updated Invoice for End of the Redisa Empire (5034) Joy Summers 05 October 2017

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Five years ago Carte Blanche raised the red flag about Redisa. Finally the minister has responded and Redisa's party is coming to an end
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have been on the story for the past five years and have the inside track on the latest developments that vindicate our story by a cabinet minister
metadata.Summary: On the 30th May, Minister Edna Molewa left for Brazil. When she arrived, she had an urgent matter to attend to at the SA consulate in Sao Paulo. She was about to sign nearly 300 pages of an urgent notice of motion to liquidate Redisa, the tyre recycling plan led by its CEO Hermann Erdmann. By signing the papers the minister began a process to dismantle the plan that she had signed into being in 2012 and defended vigorously until Carte Blanche exposed Redisa for the sham it was in 2015
metadata.Further information: The minister was so concerned about the public funds that she told the court that she had reason to believe that Erdmann would contravene the plan by dissipating public funds still under its control as well as the assets of Redisa. “I fear” says the minister “that large amounts of public funds have already been misappropriated” The court granted the provisional liquidation order and on Friday the 2nd June the liquidators marched into the plush Redisa offices, froze the bank accounts and took control of the tyre recycling plan. As it turned out Redisa’s Erdmann, had been trying to move over R200 million rand out of the bank accounts. The DEA and the liquidators stopped some of the money transfers but not all of them. But it looks like the party is over for Erdmann and his coterie of directors who have lived it up over the last three years, courtesy of the South African taxpayer. But the minister was not yet finished with Hermann Erdmann and his directors. Each year a private for profit management company Kusaga Taka takes around 20% or about a R100 million a year to manage the operations of the tyre recycling plan. Since our expose in 2015, DDG Mark Gordon has been trying to get the contract between Redisa and KT and a number of other documents. Redisa has flat out refused. But it’s in this company where the bodies are buried and so on Friday the 9th June the court granted the DEA a second provisional liquidation of Kusaga Taka. Reliable sources confirm that Erdmann had a fit and had to be escorted out of the Sunclaire offices on Friday afternoon. But more is to come as revelations from the DEA’s investigations are revealed. Carte Blanche updates this 5 year investigation as it appears that Erdmann and his directors are running out of options.
